title: What can you do when someone teases you?
examples: What should I do when someone teases me?
Is teasing the same as bullying?
How do I respond to mean jokes?

explain.say: Here is something tricky: some teasing is fun, and some really hurts. How can you tell? Look at the board. In friendly teasing, both people laugh, and it stops when you ask.

draw.text: What can you do when someone teases you?

explain.say: Friendly teasing is about small things, between friends who like each other. Now look at the hurtful group: only one person laughs, it keeps going, or it is about your looks or your family. Can you spot the difference?
If teasing hurts, here is a plan. First, stay calm and breathe. Teasers often want a big reaction, so a calm face takes away their fun. Can you show me your calm face?

steps.note: Breathe. Do not show a big reaction.

steps.note: "That is not funny to me. Stop."

explain.say: Then say how you feel, firmly: that is not funny to me, stop. Or use a little humour, like, okay, whatever, and move on. Then walk away to friends or an adult. Which would you try?

explain.say: And if it keeps happening, tell a trusted adult like a parent or teacher, because repeated teasing can become bullying. Great work! Remember, you never deserve to be made fun of.

faq.q: What can I say when someone teases me?
faq.a: Try: That is not funny to me. Please stop. Or a calm: Okay, whatever. Then move away. Short and calm works best.
asks: Tell me about the Say how you feel

faq.a: When it is on purpose, keeps happening after you ask them to stop, and is meant to hurt. Then tell a trusted adult.
asks: Tell me about the Tell if it continues

faq.a: Light joking between friends, where both people laugh and it stops when someone asks. It should never be about things that really hurt.
asks: Tell me about the Friendly teasing

faq.a: Teasing where only one person laughs, it does not stop, or it is about looks, family, culture or things you cannot change.
asks: Tell me about the Hurtful teasing

faq.q: What if I teased someone and hurt them?
faq.a: Say a real sorry, stop the teasing, and next time check: are we both laughing? Everyone gets it wrong sometimes.
asks: I think I hurt my friend with a joke

facts: Counsellors often say a teasing comment is only friendly if both people find it funny and it stops when asked.
Teasing that is repeated and meant to hurt is one of the most common forms of bullying.

quiz.say: Your friend jokes about your shoes, sees you are upset, and stops. This is…

options.show: Friendly teasing that went a bit far, then stopped
options.say: Friendly teasing that went a bit far, then stopped

quiz.why: It stopped when you were upset, so it was not bullying; you can still say it hurt.

wrong.2: It is still fine to say how you felt.

quiz.say: Someone keeps calling you names every day after you asked them to stop. What should you do?
quiz.why: Repeated, hurtful teasing is bullying, and adults can help stop it.

wrong.1: Name-calling back can make things worse.
wrong.2: Keeping it secret lets it carry on.
